_comment: The four lords of the realm, once, for every campaign. A campaign's provinces.json only names which of them holds a realm ('lord': 'margrave'); nothing about a lord is written twice. Each keeps the personality of one of Lords of the Realm II's four (Knight, Baron, Countess, Bishop) under a title of our own. 'offersAllianceEvery' is the original's (12/10/8/4 turns); 'grudgeLimit' — how many turns of alliance he stomachs before the grudge breaks it — is not known from the original and is ours [I]. 'letters' are what he writes back, by what he is answering; {gold} is filled with a gift's size.

letters.gift-thanks: Your {gold} crowns are received. A soldier does not forget who paid his men.
letters.gift-slight: You sent me less than you have sent before. I count, my lord. Everyone in a camp counts.
letters.compliment-pleased: Kind words. I will have them read to the men at supper.
letters.compliment-weary: Enough letters. Send me something I can feed a horse on.
letters.insult: Say it to my face, on a field of your choosing. I will be there before you.
letters.alliance-yes: Your counsel is good. We will fight together, and we shall win together.
letters.alliance-no: I do not put my banner beside a man I do not yet know. Not this year.
letters.alliance-offer: My lord, the roads are dangerous and we both keep an army on them. Let them march the same way.
letters.alliance-broken: I have carried you long enough. From this day my men march for me alone.
letters.alliance-ended: So be it. I will remember who broke faith first.
letters.help-yes: My men are already saddled. Tell me where the enemy stands.
letters.help-no: I cannot spare a lance this season. Hold your walls.
letters.attack-yes: A fair request. I will ride on them before the season is out.
letters.attack-no: I will not throw my men at that gate for another lord's quarrel.
letters.warning: You try my patience, my lord. The next insult is answered with steel.
letters.war: Enough. From today there is war between us, and it ends with one of us.

letters.gift-thanks: {gold} crowns. The border is an expensive thing to keep, and you have helped keep it.
letters.gift-slight: A smaller purse than last time. Is the Crown poorer, or am I worth less to it?
letters.compliment-pleased: The March has few friends. It is good to hear from one.
letters.compliment-weary: Your clerk writes well. My walls are not built of letters.
letters.insult: I have hanged men on the border for less than you have written.
letters.alliance-yes: Your counsel is good. We will fight together, and we shall win together.
letters.alliance-no: The March stands alone until I have reason to think otherwise.
letters.alliance-offer: Two lords watching the same road should watch it together. What say you?
letters.alliance-broken: Our friendship has cost me more than it has paid. The March stands alone again.
letters.alliance-ended: You break your word lightly. The March will not forget it.
letters.help-yes: The Watch will come. See that there is bread for them when they arrive.
letters.help-no: My own border is burning. I have no men to send you.
letters.attack-yes: They have been a thorn in the March for years. Gladly.
letters.attack-no: I have no quarrel with them yet, and I will not buy one for you.
letters.warning: Mind your words. The March has a long memory and a short temper.
letters.war: You have made an enemy on your northern border. Sleep lightly.

letters.gift-thanks: How generous — {gold} crowns. I shall think of you warmly, and often.
letters.gift-slight: A lighter gift than your last. I do notice these things, my lord.
letters.compliment-pleased: You flatter me, and I allow it. Do write again.
letters.compliment-weary: Sweet words go stale when there are too many of them.
letters.insult: How very common of you. I had expected better manners from a crown.
letters.alliance-yes: Your counsel is good. We will fight together, and we shall win together.
letters.alliance-no: I am touched, but I do not bind myself so easily.
letters.alliance-offer: My lord, we would do better as friends than as neighbours. Shall we be friends?
letters.alliance-broken: I find our arrangement no longer suits me. Do not take it to heart.
letters.alliance-ended: How disappointing. I had thought better of you.
letters.help-yes: Of course. My captains will be with you shortly.
letters.help-no: I would love to, truly, but my own lands need every man I have.
letters.attack-yes: They have been tiresome. I will see to it.
letters.attack-no: I have no wish to make that enemy. Ask me something else.
letters.warning: You are making this very difficult, my lord. Do take care.
letters.war: Then you leave me no choice. Consider us at war.

letters.gift-thanks: {gold} crowns for the abbey. Heaven sees what you give, my son, and so do I.
letters.gift-slight: Less than you gave before. The Lord loves a cheerful giver, and a consistent one.
letters.compliment-pleased: Bless you, my son. You shall be remembered at Vespers.
letters.compliment-weary: Flattery is a small sin, but you commit it very often.
letters.insult: I will pray for you. Pray that it is all I do.
letters.alliance-yes: Your counsel is good. We will fight together, and we shall win together.
letters.alliance-no: The abbey does not yet trust you, my son. Show us a better heart.
letters.alliance-offer: My son, the abbey has need of friends in these wicked times. Will you be one?
letters.alliance-broken: The brothers and I have prayed on it. We can no longer stand beside you.
letters.alliance-ended: You break a vow as easily as bread. God is watching, my son.
letters.help-yes: The abbey's men will march under the cross to your side.
letters.help-no: Our men are few and our walls are old. We cannot come.
letters.attack-yes: Their lord is no friend of the Church. It shall be done.
letters.attack-no: I will not bless that war. Find another sword.
letters.warning: Repent, my son, while there is still time to.
letters.war: You are cast out. Let every man of the abbey take up arms against you.
